acceptance.criterion_verbatim: A controlled STALE partition produces a visibly different state (marker/refusal), not silently older numbers. Resolve the TRADING CALENDAR first (NEVER#1) -- count trading days via lib/trading_calendar.py; a wall-clock check false-alarms every Monday
acceptance.invocation: test_AC4_ARM1_marker_a_stale_partition_reads_STALE_not_silently_older; test_AC4_ARM2_refusal; test_AC4_NEVER1_friday_is_mondays_answer -- all on lib.trading_calendar; PLUS the carrier arms -- test_CARRIER_the_SAME_stored_payload_yields_DIFFERENT_verdicts_as_now_moves, test_CARRIER_a_baked_verdict_is_REFUSED_and_the_guard_can_fail, test_CARRIER_the_refusal_arm_still_refuses_THROUGH_the_carrier, test_CARRIER_does_not_convert_a_calendar_daily_feed_into_a_build_cadence
acceptance.output_evidence: BOTH ARMS EXERCISED, AND THE CALENDAR WAS RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT BEFORE THE POLICY WAS WRITTEN. NEVER#1 FIRST: the partition cadence was MEASURED against the live bucket rather than assumed -- 2026-08-22 (Saturday) and 2026-08-23 (Sunday) BOTH carry the full detail artifact, 8002 bytes each, LastModified ~06:00Z via s3api (UTC; the decomp's '~02:00Z' is the same instant in ET). THIS FEED LANDS EVERY CALENDAR DAY, WEEKENDS INCLUDED. That measurement is what selects the basis: a calendar-day check would alarm on a Saturday for a feed whose business content cannot have changed, whereas the trading-day frontier is correct on both arms with NO special case. Exercised: vintage('2026-08-21' Friday, now=Saturday 08-22) -> FRESH, and now=Sunday 08-23 -> FRESH, because expected_last_trading_day returns FRIDAY on a non-trading day -- FRIDAY IS MONDAY'S ANSWER, mechanically. now=Monday 08-24 -> STALE, trading_days_behind=1. A NAIVE WALL-CLOCK CHECK WOULD HAVE CALLED FRIDAY STALE ON SATURDAY, and the test asserts that gap is 1 calendar day so the false alarm it avoids is EXHIBITED rather than described. ARM 1 (marker): as_of 2026-08-27 -> FRESH/0; as_of 2026-08-25 -> STALE/2; the states DIFFER, so a consumer can reject on it. ARM 2 (refusal): assert_fresh raises SatelliteWeightError('STALE PARTITION: ...') on the stale date and returns FRESH on the current one. freshness_basis='trading-day-frontier' rides on the face of every result, so a consumer never has to guess which clock produced the verdict. RESIDUAL NAMED, NOT GLOSSED: SAT-a-4 is unmade, and a build-time constant would carry the vintage of the BUILD rather than of the data -- vintage() would then be measuring the wrong clock while still returning FRESH. That is stated in the module, and the staleness arm must be RE-EXERCISED at whatever boundary COO chooses. || RE-EXERCISED THROUGH THE CARRIER after 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z's 18:21Z SAT-a-4 ruling, which ruled OUT the build-time-constant class, LEFT THE FORM TO THIS SEAT, and required in terms: 'the staleness arm MUST be re-exercised at that boundary ... THE CARRIER IS EXACTLY WHAT THE TEST WAS NOT VARYING.' IT IS NOW VARIED. THE CHOSEN CONTRACT: the artifact carries `as_of` (a FACT, claim measured, it does not age) and THE READER COMPUTES THE VERDICT via vintage(as_of, now) at read time. ⛔ THE RULED-OUT CLASS IS WIDER THAN THE NAMED FORM AND THAT IS THE DESIGN: a served block that STAMPS `state: FRESH` at PRODUCE time fails IDENTICALLY to a build-time constant -- true when written, ageing silently -- so the payload is FORBIDDEN from carrying a verdict and `assert_no_baked_verdict` ENFORCES it, making the defect INEXPRESSIBLE rather than discouraged. THE DISCRIMINATING TEST: ONE set of stored bytes, `now` moved and nothing else -- read(block, 2026-08-27) -> FRESH/0 and read(block, 2026-08-31) -> STALE/2, with as_of and rows asserted IDENTICAL across both. A build-time constant and a stamped block both return the same verdict forever; this asserts the opposite property, so if anyone later bakes `state` in, THIS test fails rather than a style review catching it. THE GUARD MADE TO FAIL ON DEMAND: three baked fields (state, trading_days_behind, freshness_basis) each raise, on assert_no_baked_verdict AND on read(), with the clean payload as the POSITIVE CONTROL that does not raise. COO'S NEVER#1 RIDER IS ALSO EXERCISED ('a weekly-built constant against a daily-landing feed is the same defect wearing a different hat'): the payload records NO produce-time field at all -- `checked_at` is in CARRIER_FORBIDDEN_FIELDS -- so there is nothing to convert into a build cadence, and Friday's payload read on Saturday and Sunday is FRESH while Monday is STALE, the weekend arms surviving the new boundary intact. FORM-AGNOSTIC ON PURPOSE: served block, portal fetch or API response all satisfy this contract and all fail it identically if they stamp a verdict -- it rules out the CLASS, which is what was ruled, rather than picking a transport this lane does not own.
acceptance.denominator: 2 weekend partitions head-checked (both present, 8002 bytes each); 5 (as_of, now) pairs exercised directly plus 7 THROUGH the carrier; 1 payload read at 2 different `now` values yielding 2 different verdicts from identical bytes; 3 baked-verdict fields each refused on 2 call paths, against 1 clean positive control
